summary: Inspected existing JobManager and MCP dispatch to evaluate operator proposal for automatic promotion of slow tool calls to jobs. Current Client/Modules/JobManager.fs handles only OS Process records in client memory, with stdout/stderr events and max 100 retained completed jobs; GetJobResult is itself forwarded to the client. Server/McpTools.send awaits ClientService.SendCommandToUser, which currently waits for SignalR ReceiveCommand callback/response and couples waits to HTTP RequestAborted. Client/Program.fs registers ReceiveCommand task callback that executes the command and sends reply before completion. Recommended a shared, bounded, authenticated asynchronous tool-operation registry: fast path returns regular result, slow path returns jobId and existing stable operationId after short threshold, and polling returns original typed AgentCommandResponse with errors/instructions/state effects. Server-side polling must not route through the same potentially blocked SignalR client; detach from HTTP aborted token only after explicit durable admission, ensure ledger idempotency/uncertain outcome recovery and correct device/agent isolation; still fix root cause of client receive-loop head-of-line blocking. No source/task changes or deployment; conceptual analysis only.
nextAction: Operator: if desired, authorize expanding the existing P2 investigation task task-b0e62987fa03497a809a7d1bdd700ae4 to include an automatically promoted, server-managed generic tool-job facility. Design must preserve normal quick tool responses, explicitly pending jobs, and exact operation-ID correctness; measure and eliminate receive-loop head-of-line blocking independently. No other action required.
